_meta.changelog_1_5_50: Suite 083d (loyalty missions E2E) fixture set: MSN_E2E_RUN + MSN_E2E_{ORDERVALUE,ORDERCOUNT,PERSKU,PERSKU_PTS} + MSN_E2E_PRODUCT_{UNIT,A,B,PTS} + MSN_E2E_REWARD_USER. Run REG-2026-08-28-1154 returned 2 PASS / 6 BLOCKED because the shared MSN_* missions had been CONSUMED — MSN_ORDERCOUNT at 2 of 2 Completed, MSN_ORDERVALUE at 5,842,446/100% — and a Completed mission stops accruing entirely (proven by a control pair inside one order: MSN_ZEROTARGET 24 -> 25 while MSN_ORDERCOUNT stayed frozen at 2). Mission progress is per-(user,mission), cumulative, monotonic, frozen at completion, with NO reset path in vc-module-loyalty, so repeatability comes from minting a FRESH mission per run (name carries a run handle) rather than from resetting anything. Products are stable and NOT run-scoped (no per-user state), packSize 1 (MSN_PERSKU_PRODUCT_B steps 0->2->0, so "quantity exactly 1" was unachievable) and trackInventory=false. MSN_E2E_PRODUCT_PTS is the first PerSku target priced in the loyalty currency, which is what makes the no-currency-filter question (LoyaltyMissionLogicService.cs:~416 vs LoyaltyProgramHandler.cs:199) askable at all. MSN_E2E_REWARD_USER borrows the per-run ephemeral LOYALTY_ZERO_USER because a 500-PTS reward against LOYALTY_VIP_USER (964,189,233 PTS) cannot demonstrate that the points spent were earned from a mission. Seeder scripts/seed-data/loyalty/seed-missions-e2e.mjs, spec module missions-e2e-specs.mjs, guard npm run td:validate:missions-e2e (a VACUITY guard: it fails when a fixture was not pre-completion at seed time or when the reward stops being legible against the balance).
_meta.changelog_1_5_51: Suite 083d per-case split: MSN_E2E_ORDERVALUE_{003,005,006,008} + MSN_E2E_USER_{003,005,006,008}. MSN_E2E_ORDERVALUE served five cases and FOUR of them also shared one account (LOYALTY_VIP_USER); that shared ACCOUNT was the defect. LoyaltyMissionLogicService.ProcessOrderAsync runs once per order INSERT and advances EVERY mission applicable to that order's user, so four missions on one account are all moved by any one case's order — minting more missions on a shared account multiplies the rows an order touches instead of isolating anything. Evidence from the same env: run REG-2026-08-28-1154 granted 750+450+550+400 from the single order CO260828-00001, and its control pair showed MSN_ZEROTARGET advancing 24 -> 25 in that same order. Progress is keyed per-(user,mission) and MSN-E2E-004 already proved the correct axis — same mission definition, own account, never contended — so each of 003/005/006/008 now has its own per-run account (AGENT-TEST-msne2e-*, a sweep namespace deliberately DISJOINT from seed-loyalty-ephemeral-user.mjs's AGENT-TEST-loyzero-* so that seeder's teardown cannot delete them mid-run). MSN_E2E_ORDERVALUE is now MSN-E2E-004 only. Per-case MISSIONS are still required, for SIZING rather than isolation: under .claude/rules/test-data.md SECOND RULE each target must be placed so a wrong implementation of ITS link produces a different observation, and the four placements conflict (003 between merchandise and total; 005 between the same cart's discounted and undiscounted totals; 006 and 008 below EVERY candidate reading so a card short of 100% cannot be ambiguous between their own question and a measurement question; 008 additionally low enough that its own order completes no sibling, or the reward delta it asserts on names nothing). EVERY per-case target is MEASURED, not modelled — goal_target is a RUNTIME field. vcst-qa applies a 20% tax to (subTotal - discount + shipping) that nothing in this repo had declared, and it is the only reason merchandise value and order total differ at all when shipping is 0. Measured through the storefront xAPI 2026-08-28: 9 units -> subTotal 45 / tax 9 / TOTAL 54; 10 units -> 50 / 10 / 60; 10 units + 20% coupon -> 50 / disc 10 / tax 8 / TOTAL 48. The previous fixture's modelled discount_post_total of 40 is 8.00 away from the platform's real 48 — four times the band it was meant to discriminate inside. The seeder therefore builds each case's cart on that case's own account and derives the target from what came back; a target that cannot be placed in a real band fails the SEED rather than the suite. Rewards are DIVERGENT and mnemonic (503/505/506/508): four missions sharing a 500-PTS reward are indistinguishable in a balance delta or a points-history row, so "the grant came from THIS mission" would be unfalsifiable. STATED LIMIT: attribution is exact only WITHIN this fixture set. Other store-wide missions still grant on a fresh account's first order (MSN_ZEROTARGET OrderCountGoal 0 reward 200, and the count-1 fixtures), so BAL_1 - BAL_0 = reward is FALSE on this env for any account; the seeder measures that co-grant set live and records co_completing_missions / reward_expected_total, which is what a delta assertion must use. Seeder scripts/seed-data/loyalty/seed-missions-e2e.mjs, spec module missions-e2e-specs.mjs, shared account mechanics scripts/lib/loyalty-ephemeral-account.mjs, guard npm run td:validate:missions-e2e.

Previously the column existed but every row left it blank, so the seeded outcome was status=null on all of them and the per-org status a case asserted was really a property of the CONTACT (ResolveEffectiveStatus falls through to member status) — invisible from the fixture row, and liable to change meaning if the contact were ever edited. WHAT CHANGED, per source: organization-memberships.csv MOM-001..006 → Approved (effective status UNCHANGED — null + contact-Approved already resolved to Approved — only its provenance is now declared, so no existing consumer moves: MULTI_ORG_TF_BR is read by 9 suite CSVs and stays able to sign in); b2b/users.csv 19 membership-creating rows → Approved, while USR-022 (invitation-pending) and USR-025 (ORG_ASSOC_ONLY_NO_GLOBAL) keep a BLANK cell because their empty `roles` cell means the seeder creates NO membership row at all and a status there would be inert; white-labeling/users.csv all 6 → Approved. THREE NEW BLOCKING-STATUS FIXTURES on dedicated single-org accounts, because Invited/Rejected/Deleted BLOCK org sign-in and must never be a repurposed happy-path account: ORG_TF_MBR_INVITED (MOM-007), ORG_TF_MBR_REJECTED (MOM-008), ORG_TF_MBR_DELETED (MOM-009) — TechFlow / org-employee / unlocked, with the CONTACT at Approved so a refusal is provably the per-org override winning rather than a global block, and SINGLE-org so a healthy second org cannot mask the refusal via the fall-through path (which is why neither MULTI_ORG_TF_BR nor _ALT can serve these). They are AT-REST representatives, complementing ORG_TF_ONLY_STATUS which MUTATES itself through the same values mid-run. All four legal values now have a seeded representative, so no branch of MembershipStatuses.IsBlocking lacks a fixture. VOCABULARY GROUNDED IN TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES (not memory), both re-verified 2026-08-03 and agreeing: SOURCE vc-module-customer@2605501d984ab747b839b0aec16595c7674a967e (PR #312) ModuleConstants.MembershipStatuses — note it is NOT on `dev`, where the class does not exist at all, so the commit pin is load-bearing — and LIVE `GET /api/platform/settings/Customer.OrganizationMembershipStatuses` on vcst @ VirtoCommerce.Customer 3.1021.0-pr-312-2605 → allowedValues [Invited, Approved, Rejected, Deleted] with defaultValue "Approved", which is WHY Approved is the happy-path default rather than an arbitrary pick. Deliberately NOT the Customer.ContactStatuses vocabulary, which allows SIX values on the same env (Deleted, New, Locked, Invited, Rejected, Approved) — a contact status is not a membership status, and copying across the two is exactly how "Locked"/"New" end up silently non-blocking (absent from BlockingStatuses). GATE: findStatusProblems() now also fails a blank status on a membership-creating row and a status declared on a row that creates none (inert, and it reads as coverage that does not exist); it still fails an illegal value and a `;`-form arity mismatch, and WARNS on a blocking value. New side-effect-free predicates rowCreatesMembership()/statusCoverage() — `roleCol` gates them, because the seeder drops any org/role pair without a role, which is precisely how a no-membership fixture is built. The no-per-org-override cell is NOT lost by requiring a status: the VCST-5281 test model reduces membership-row-EXISTENCE out as a dependent axis ("subsumed by which side of ?? supplied the value") and covers it at D14 through ORG_ASSOC_ONLY_NO_GLOBAL, which has no membership row whatsoever. The WIRE behaviour of blank is unchanged (⇒ null, key omitted) so a re-seed can still HEAL a row back to no-override; what is now forbidden is a COMMITTED row DECLARING blank. Unit tests: scripts/unit/membership-status.test.mjs + the new membership-status-required.test.mjs (which reads the real CSVs, so the fixture set itself is gated, not just the predicates). Seeded and verified live on vcst 2026-08-03.

_meta.changelog_1_5_49: VCST-5319 Loyalty Missions (VirtoCommerce.Loyalty 3.1006.0-pr-14-1be7) — first fixture set for the Missions feature. 12 aliases: MSN_STORE_SETTINGS (the Loyalty.Missions.Enable gate + the OBSERVED value of the base Loyalty.Enable switch), MSN_PERSKU_PRODUCT_A/_B (two live-discovered catalog products shared by the PerSku pair), and 9 missions — MSN_ORDERVALUE, MSN_ORDERVALUE_ALTCURRENCY, MSN_ORDERCOUNT, MSN_PERSKU_ALL, MSN_PERSKU_ANY, MSN_PUBLISHED_PRIVATE, MSN_ZEROTARGET, MSN_ZEROREWARD, MSN_DRAFT. Source of truth: scripts/seed-data/loyalty/missions-specs.mjs (side-effect-free); seeder seed-loyalty-missions.mjs; drift guard td:validate:missions; unit tests scripts/unit/loyalty-missions-specs.test.mjs. NO GUIDs in this base file — every mission id, product id/sku and the per-env store id live in aliases.<env>.json. THREE API FACTS the fixtures are shaped around, verified live on vcst-qa 2026-08-27 and cross-checked against source: (1) a PerSkuGoal carries NO inline items — the SKU targets are a separate LoyaltyMissionGoalItem entity keyed by missionId, so a mission-only seed produces a permanently uncompletable PerSku mission that passes every existence check; (2) a Published mission is IMMUTABLE (only Published -> Archived) and cannot be un-published, so idempotency is signature-compare-then-delete-and-recreate, never repair-in-place; (3) a mission can be created directly as Published. FOUR BEHAVIOURS worth knowing when authoring cases, all observed live: StartDate > EndDate is ACCEPTED SILENTLY (no validation at save); an unrecognised status string is ACCEPTED (no status vocabulary validation); the immutability refusal comes back as HTTP 500, not 4xx; and GET /api/loyalty-missions/{id} answers 200 + a null body for a missing id rather than 404. Server-side validators that DO exist (all HTTP 400): name required, store required, at least one condition, exactly one goal, at least one reward, and CURRENCY CODE REQUIRED ON AN ORDER-VALUE GOAL. That last one contradicts the DTO: OrderValueGoal.currencyCode is `nullable` in the published Swagger, but null AND "" are both rejected 400 — so a currency-agnostic order-value mission is NOT expressible, and the original C19 plan of leaving it null is impossible. The validation is also ASYMMETRIC: presence is enforced, validity is not ("XYZ" and lowercase "usd" persist verbatim), so a wrong-currency defect cannot surface at save time. Hence the MSN_ORDERVALUE / MSN_ORDERVALUE_ALTCURRENCY pair — identical threshold and reward, differing ONLY in currency — which moves C19 to accrual time where it is answerable. Both resolve their currency from the STORE (defaultCurrency / currencies) at seed time into the per-env overlay; neither commits a literal. NOT validated at save either: a negative goal value, a negative order count, and a negative reward are all accepted. TARGETING is group-only (UserGroupIsCondition.groups: string[]) — there is NO customer-id condition anywhere in the module, so a single-customer mission is not expressible.

MULTI_ORG_TF_BR is reserved for the BACKEND lane (token-grant matrix); MULTI_ORG_TF_BR_ALT is reserved for the FRONTEND lane (storefront journeys). Why sharing the two ORGS is safe while sharing the ACCOUNT is not: an OrganizationMembership row is keyed on (userId, organizationId) and carries the per-org `status` + `isLocked` the run mutates, so two accounts in the same two orgs own fully independent rows; the global contact `status` the ResolveEffectiveStatus fallback reads is per-CONTACT, also independent. The lanes only READ the orgs. ORG-LEVEL BASELINE observed read-only on vcst 2026-08-03 (the deciding variable when no membership row exists — org-scoped permissions then collapse to Organization.Roles): TechFlow Organization.Roles = [purchasing-agent, org-employee] (2), org status=null; BuildRight Organization.Roles = [] (EMPTY). ORG STATUS IS SHARED, MUTABLE STATE AND WAS OBSERVED DRIFTING MID-RUN: BuildRight read status=Active at ~12:5x UTC and status=Approved at 13:29:46Z the same day (modifiedBy=admin, the shared account) — NOT written by any seeder here (the cross-org seed path never touches an org; seedOrgs is only reached via seedOrgGraph). Treat org status as a live value to READ at test time, never as a seeded constant — and see the caveat below on org-level state. An EMPTY Organization.Roles means a token with no membership row carries ZERO org-scoped permissions in BuildRight — do not read that as a product failure. Nothing here was written: Organization.Roles, org status, Customer.ContactDefaultStatus/OrganizationDefaultStatus and the OrganizationRolesWhitelist/MembershipRolesWhitelist module settings were left untouched by the seed. THE ONE THING THIS DOES NOT PROTECT: a test that mutates the ORG entity itself (org status/rename) or DELETES an org — e.g. checklist condition #45 'stale invite after org deleted' — is org-level shared state and must use its own throwaway AGENT-TEST org, not TechFlow/BuildRight. AUTH: /connect/token password grant needs storeId=B2B-store (camelCase) alongside organization_id (snake_case) for an org-scoped grant; a grant WITHOUT storeId fails outright — observed live on vcst 2026-08-03: HTTP 400 `invalid_grant` (MULTI_ORG_TF_BR's older note records `user_cannot_login_in_store`; the code differs by platform version, the failure does not). So @td(MULTI_ORG_TF_BR_ALT.store_id) is load-bearing, not decorative. Baseline after seed: both memberships declare membership_status=Approved EXPLICITLY (organization-memberships.csv MOM-003/MOM-004) ⇒ effective status Approved in both orgs without depending on the contact's status. This changed on 2026-08-03: the baseline used to be status=null, which resolved to Approved only by falling through to the contact — so the per-org status a case asserted was really a property of a different entity. ORG_ASSOC_ONLY_NO_GLOBAL._comment: VCST-5281 / B2C-MBR-040 (F8b) — the LEGACY-ASSOCIATION fixture: an AGENT-TEST contact with Contact.Status=Approved, associated with BOTH TechFlow and BuildRight through `contact.organizations` ONLY, holding ZERO OrganizationMembership rows and EMPTY global ApplicationUser.Roles. This is the shape 104 of the 105 at-risk accounts on this env have. Recipe: test-data/b2b/contacts.csv CON-025 + test-data/b2b/users.csv USR-025 (roles cell EMPTY) → seed with `TEST_ENV=<env> node scripts/seed-data/b2b/seed-company-users.mjs b2b --only USR-025`. The empty `roles` cell is the MECHANISM: provisionContactLogins pairs each org with its index-parallel role and filters out any org without one, so no role ⇒ no membership row, while seedContacts still writes both org associations and contactBody forces status=Approved. stripSeededGlobalRoles runs on every login, and the account is created with no roles at all. Runtime GUIDs (`userId`, `contactId`) live in aliases.<env>.json only; the two org ids are pinned inline (seedOrgs forces body.id = organizations.csv platform_id ⇒ identical on every env, DV-021 allowlist). Password {{DEFAULT_TEST_PASSWORD}}. AGENT-TEST- prefix on both the email and the member name ⇒ swept by `npm run seed:b2b:teardown`.
ORG_ASSOC_ONLY_NO_GLOBAL._notes: TWO LOAD-BEARING PROPERTIES — ADDING EITHER ONE DESTROYS THIS FIXTURE. (1) ZERO OrganizationMembership rows. (2) EMPTY global ApplicationUser.Roles. B2C-MBR-040 asserts the BL-B2B-007 three-term permission union — org-level Organization.Roles ∪ membership OrganizationMembership.Roles ∪ global ApplicationUser.Roles. With no membership row the membership term is empty, and with no global role the global term is empty, so the ORG-LEVEL term is the only one left and becomes observable for the first time. A future re-seed must NOT 'helpfully' add a membership row or a role: a role in users.csv USR-025 makes provisionContactLogins create a membership (td:validate:b2b check [4] now hard-fails that combination via the ASSOCIATION-ONLY marker), and a global role reintroduces exactly the defect that makes {{MULTI_ORG_USER_EMAIL}} useless here — that account has a global org-maintainer role, which yields an INVARIANT 11 permissions across five different org claims (including orgs whose Organization.Roles is empty), completely masking the org-level term. Every b2b/users.csv account with a role fails property 1 by construction. membership_status is blank and MOOT here — there is no membership row to carry a status. MEASURED LIVE ON vcst 2026-08-03 (the numbers the case compares against): TechFlow Organization.Roles = [purchasing-agent, org-employee] → org-scoped token carries 2 permission claims in the `permission` claim (storefront:organization:view, storefront:user:view); BuildRight Organization.Roles = [] → 0 permission claims (the `permission` claim is ABSENT entirely, not an empty array — assert on absence-or-zero, not on an empty list); and the UNSCOPED token also carries 0, which is the proof the global term really is zero. NOTE WHY 2 AND NOT 4: purchasing-agent and org-employee grant the SAME two storefront perms (see b2b/roles.csv), so the union of the two roles is 2 distinct permissions — do not expect one-per-role. Both grants return HTTP 200. The two counts DIFFER, so the org-level term IS flowing into the org-scoped JWT — no BL-B2B-007 / VCST-5239 regression on this env at this build. Note the absolute numbers are 2/0, NOT the 11→12 recorded in BL-B2B-007: that 11 was the global-role baseline of a DIFFERENT account, so 11→12 is not the oracle for this fixture; the oracle is 'TechFlow > BuildRight, and BuildRight == 0'.

LOCKOUT_TEST_USERS._comment: Sprint 26-10 Batch-B dedicated lockout test accounts. CREATED on vcst-qa 2026-05-29 via POST /api/platform/security/users/create (idempotent — re-check GET /api/platform/security/users/{login} before recreating). These are AGENT-TEST-* self-provisioned throwaway accounts, swept by /qa-seed-data teardown; passwords are NOT stored here (throwaway test creds, consistent with test-data/users/agent-user-pool.csv) — the SETUP blocks set them: sf=ValidLockPw1!, admin=ValidLockPw1!, unlock=ValidUnlockPw1!, manager=ValidMgrPw1!, target=ValidLockPw1!. Consumers: sf -> suite 031 AUTH-070 (Customer-type storefront user; back-office Administrator users cannot authenticate against the storefront per reference_admin_backoffice_only — so this one is intentionally Customer-type with a linked contact memberId 154c045b-91e3-4915-ad0b-8b981557feb1). admin -> 020 PLAT-081. unlock -> 020 PLAT-082. manager (Manager-type, VCST-4999) -> 020 PLAT-083. target -> 049 API-036. No special permissions assigned (permissions live on Roles per feedback_admin_permissions_via_roles; assign a role to the user record if a case needs one). OBSERVED LOCK CONTRACT (verified 2026-05-29 on the unlock user, platform OAuth + Identity Framework): (a) ADMIN API LOCK — POST /api/platform/security/users/{id}/lock -> {succeeded:true}; GET .../users/{id}/locked -> {locked:true}; user record lockoutEnd='9999-12-31T23:59:59.9999999+00:00' (permanent sentinel) + lockoutEnabled=true. UNLOCK — POST .../users/{id}/unlock -> {succeeded:true}; /locked -> {locked:false}; lockoutEnd resets to '0001-01-01T00:00:00+00:00' (epoch min) + lockoutEnabled stays true. (b) FAILED-LOGIN LOCK — 5+ bad-password POST /connect/token (invalid_grant each) auto-locks: /locked -> {locked:true} with a FINITE timed lockoutEnd (now+window, NOT the 9999 sentinel) + accessFailedCount resets to 0 once locked. Distinguish: admin-lock = 9999 sentinel (permanent); failed-login lock = finite timed window. status/UserState remains null in both (platform persists lock via Identity lockoutEnd, not a UserState enum — same as IMPERSONATE_TARGET_BLOCKED). Use @td(LOCKOUT_TEST_USERS.unlock_id) etc. instead of hardcoding the GUID/login in cases.

LOYALTY_ZERO_USER._notes: EMPTY-BY-DESIGN base values: email/memberId/securityAccountId are all RUN-variant and are supplied by aliases.<env>.json when the seeder runs. Per the multi-env rule an unseeded env therefore resolves them to an empty string - a CLEAR MISS that fails loudly at sign-in - rather than a stale or wrong-env value. EPHEMERAL, PER-RUN, GENUINELY ZERO-BALANCE loyalty user. Provisioned by npm run seed:loyalty:zero-user (scripts/seed-data/loyalty/seed-loyalty-ephemeral-user.mjs) and swept by --teardown. NO fields are pinned here on purpose: the email is RUN-variant (AGENT-TEST-loyzero-<utc>-<rand>@test-agent.com) and the ids are runtime GUIDs, so all three live only in aliases.<env>.json. An unseeded env therefore resolves them to '' (a clear miss) rather than a stale value. WHY IT EXISTS: a loyalty balance CANNOT be reset (vc-module-loyalty exposes the op-log read-only; no balance set/debit), so the shared LOYALTY_NOBAL_USER drifts upward every time a case earns points - it reached 1,044 PTS by 2026-08-05, above the dearest PTS catalog item (PTS344), which made MCO-E2E-002 unable to produce a shortfall at qty 1 and silently PASS while testing nothing. A fresh account starts at 0, so ANY PTS line at qty 1 is a guaranteed shortfall - deterministic, and parallel-safe (no contention between runners). PROVEN 2026-08-05: a fresh user with groups=[] and organizations=[] authenticates, reports currentBalance 0, and sees 39 PTS-priced products - PTS pricing is catalog-scoped (the price list is assigned by catalogId, not memberId), so no VIP group is required for PTS VISIBILITY. IMPORTANT: the seeder still provisions the user WITH org membership (createUser withOrg:true) because the ORG is what supplies the shipping ADDRESSES a checkout case needs - a brand-new contact has none, and without an address the cart cannot reach a decisive place-order state. Do not "simplify" this to no-org on the strength of the pricing finding. Password is DEFAULT_TEST_PASSWORD - ONE shared value, never a per-run random, and specifically the var that EXISTS in .env.playwright.local so Playwright --secrets can substitute it by NAME and redact it. A dedicated EPHEMERAL_USER_PASSWORD was removed: it is absent from the secrets file, so setting it would have silently forced the password into the transcript in plaintext. CAVEAT: deleting the account does NOT purge its loyalty op-log (read-only, no purge API) - stranded rows accumulate; harmless for balances since each new account is a new id.
